ideas.title: Fifty guards read one registry, not fifty headers and four rosters
ideas.reading: scripts/check-repo.mjs spawns 50 guards from a hand-kept table while its own line-37 comment says 43, docs/agents/repo-checks.md line 3 says 48 and line 9 says 27, and AGENTS.md line 44 says 50 — only the last is checked, by a regex over prose in scripts/check-agents.mjs lines 286–298. 27 of the 50 guards define their own walk() (471 lines across scripts/check-*.mjs), 0 import a shared walker, the skip set is restated 52 times for drizzle and 49 for coverage, and only 6 guards import any local helper at all. Per-guard metadata is scattered: 22 guard headers cite an ADR, 50 ADRs name a guard, 30 h3 sections in repo-checks.md cover 35 of 50 labels (15 have no write-up), package.json aliases 40 of 50 (check-uuid-segments.mjs, check-live-trips.mjs and 8 others cannot be run alone by name), and 11 have no test despite .claude/rules/scripts.md's 'A guard gets a test beside it'. 33 further guards are tree-scanning vitest files in src/ (src/app/instant-coverage.test.ts, src/app/shop/tenant-gate-coverage.test.ts, src/i18n/provider-coverage.test.ts) that no roster or report lists; AGENTS.md's test:changed row says 'name the three guards by path' and docs/agents/verifying.md names four. Of 90 rule bullets in .claude/rules/*.md only 7 say which guard enforces them, so a session reading a rule cannot tell remembered from mechanical. The steelman holds only in part: check-repo.mjs's header says it 'only spawns them' and per-process isolation with the 90s ceiling is worth keeping, but isolation is a property of spawning, not of hand-copied tables and walkers.
ideas.idea: One `scripts/guards.mjs` registry, one record per guard: label, script (or vitest path), the rule in one sentence, the ADR id, the repo-checks.md anchor, the roots it scans, its baseline, and kind (script|vitest). scripts/check-repo.mjs spawns from it; scripts/check-agents.mjs §7 and scripts/agent-health.mjs read it instead of readdir plus regex; `pnpm check:repo <label>` replaces the 40 package.json aliases and `pnpm check:repo --why <label>` prints the rule, ADR and doc anchor; scripts/explain-failure.mjs uses the same record to signpost a red guard. One `scripts/lib/source-files.mjs` (skip set, source predicate, ranged read) replaces the 27 walk() bodies, and the eight copy/text guards (2,823 lines) become rules over one pass. The AGENTS.md row stops carrying a number; repo-checks.md's roster paragraph is deleted and its 30 essays stay, anchored by label; the 33 vitest guards appear in the registry so the schema.ts advice in AGENTS.md and verifying.md derives from one list. The grammar afterwards: a rule bullet names its label, the label resolves to script, ADR and essay, and every roster is a view.
ideas.dissolves: The hand-kept checks table, four drifting counts, 40 package aliases, 471 lines of duplicated walkers, and the invisible second guard mechanism in src/.
ideas.scope: scripts/guards.mjs (new), scripts/lib/source-files.mjs (new), scripts/check-repo.mjs, scripts/check-agents.mjs + test, scripts/agent-health.mjs, scripts/explain-failure.mjs, 27 scripts/check-*.mjs walkers, package.json, AGENTS.md (check:repo and test:changed rows), docs/agents/repo-checks.md, docs/agents/verifying.md, .claude/rules/scripts.md, the 7 rule bullets that name guards plus the 83 that could.

ideas.title: A generated digest and a citation guard make 311 ADRs navigable
ideas.reading: docs/architecture/decisions/ holds 311 records (313 files with README.md and 0000-template.md), 395,649 words: 253 Accepted, 31 Superseded (18 'in part'), 9 Proposed; 112 landed in July, 165 in August, 28 in September. The only finder is the filename — docs/architecture/decisions/README.md says new records 'are found by descriptive filename and do not need a central index entry, avoiding merge conflicts' — its hand-kept Historical index has 6 rows, and scripts/check-adrs.mjs (55 lines, no test) validates id, status, date and four section names and nothing about reach. Filenames such as 20260906-before-you-ask.md, 20260907-nothing-from-nowhere.md, 20260908-one-hand.md, 20260911-clear-the-deck.md, 20260907-in-your-hands.md and 20260904-reef-all-the-way-down.md carry no domain noun, and 41 of 305 dated titles begin with 'A' and 17 with 'The'. Reach today: 198 of 311 ids are cited from src/, 235 from docs outside decisions/, 31 from nowhere; of 32 Superseded records naming a successor, 5 successors do not cite the record they replace. .claude/skills/adr/SKILL.md line 15 says 'Keep it under a page', yet 167 records exceed 1,000 words, 40 exceed 2,000 and 15 exceed 3,000 (largest 7,797, 20260814-self-declared-cards.md), and .claude/skills/new-feature/SKILL.md line 33 still tells a session to update an 'ADR index' the README says not to keep. The merge-conflict reason holds for a hand-edited table and not for a generated one: docs/engineering/manual-actions.md is already generated from the registry in infra/lib/infra-stack.ts, and scripts/route-coverage.json is a ledger a guard maintains.
ideas.idea: `pnpm adr [words]` (scripts/adr-digest.mjs) prints one line per record from the files themselves — id, status, the heading's decision clause, the first sentence of `## Decision`, and a cited-by count — so there is nothing to hand-edit and nothing to conflict; the same module regenerates the README's index on main in CI, replacing the 6-row historical table. scripts/check-adrs.mjs gains two invariants and a test: an Accepted record is cited from at least one file outside decisions/ (31 fail today; each gets a citation from the code it binds or becomes Deprecated), and a superseding record cites the one it supersedes (5 fail). The heading clause becomes the digest line, which gives the template's 'imperative title' rule its first reader, and the 'under a page' rule is either enforced as a `## Decision` word cap with the essay allowed beneath it or deleted from the adr skill. AGENTS.md 'Read first' gains one clause — `pnpm adr <noun>` before structural work — and the stale 'ADR index' step in new-feature is corrected. Superseded records stay, listed with their status, as the settled decision requires.
ideas.dissolves: The hand-kept Historical index, the 'found by filename' convention that poetic titles defeat, and the 31 records nothing points at.
ideas.scope: scripts/adr-digest.mjs (new) + test, scripts/check-adrs.mjs + first test, package.json (`adr`), docs/architecture/decisions/README.md, .claude/skills/adr/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/new-feature/SKILL.md line 33, AGENTS.md Read-first, .github/workflows/ci.yml (regenerate on main), the 31 orphan ADRs and 5 non-citing successors.
ideas.firstSlice: Ship scripts/adr-digest.mjs with `pnpm adr`, and add the orphan and successor invariants to check-adrs.mjs in report mode naming the 31 and the 5, with a test beside it.
ideas.conflicts: Settled: 'Superseded ADRs are retained' (docs/architecture/overview.md line 67 section) — respected, the digest lists them; #1738 (verify ADR code citations — the cited-by count is the reverse direction of the same link, and one pass can do both); #1818 (decisions recorded in code never written to docs — an orphan invariant is the general form of that complaint).

ideas.title: Four route maps become one; task:context is deleted
ideas.reading: Where a thing lives is written four times: AGENTS.md's route map (55 rows, 1,177 words, 122 literal paths), the 'Where things are' sections of .claude/rules/{surfaces,domain,db}.md (2,119 words restating 77 of those 122 paths — the staff-destinations registry is AGENTS.md line 85 and .claude/rules/domain.md line 52), scripts/task-context-data.mjs (602 lines, 14 areas, 49 of the 122 paths, 377 invariant and validate lines), and docs/README.md's 46-row map. scripts/task-context-data.mjs's validate arrays say 'pnpm check' 14 times and its shared.rules say 'then pnpm check before commit', which scripts/guard-bash.mjs line 67 refuses as a whole-suite command and AGENTS.md's hard rules forbid locally. AGENTS.md 'Read first' step 3 asks every session to run `pnpm task:context <area>`, scripts/check-agents.mjs §4 spends 15 lines keeping its paths alive, and the 14 areas map onto rules that already load themselves the moment a matching file is read. The rules exist so that 'the rules and the route-map detail for one area live there, not in AGENTS.md' (.claude/skills/README.md lines 11–13), but AGENTS.md's map is what a session reads before it knows which file to open, so the where must stay always-loaded and the rules' copy is the redundant one. A staff-page session today loads AGENTS.md 4,264 + surfaces.md 2,125 + domain.md 958 + 916 descriptions = 8,263 words, of which roughly the 77 restated paths' prose is paid twice.
ideas.idea: Delete `pnpm task:context`: scripts/task-context.mjs, scripts/task-context-data.mjs, its package script, the AGENTS.md step and command row, check-agents §4 and the .claude/settings.json allow entry; each area's invariants that are not already a rule bullet move into the matching .claude/rules file, which loads on read. The rules' 'Where things are' sections keep only what the AGENTS.md row does not say (the consumer list, the trap, the ADR), and every AGENTS.md row ends with the rule that governs it, so the grammar is: AGENTS.md says where, the rule says how and why, the guard says no. docs/README.md stays the map of documents and nothing else. The measured after: AGENTS.md loses about 70 words, and a surfaces+domain session drops the restated share of 2,119 words (estimate 1,000) with no rule lost.
ideas.dissolves: The fourth registry, one always-loaded 'Read first' step, 49 restated paths, and 14 validate lines that contradict the bash guard.

ideas.title: A skill is a trigger plus pointer; docs hold the body
ideas.reading: 20 skill bodies total 28,367 words, 8 of them over 1,300 words (debug 4,516; stacked-prs 2,817; backlog-routine 2,805; e2e-and-visual 2,210), and their descriptions are 786 of the 5,229 words every session loads. Six skills have a doc twin: .claude/skills/new-feature/SKILL.md (713 words) restates docs/engineering/workflow.md (697) as 'the executable order' and its step 7 names an 'ADR index' the ADR README says not to keep; verify (1,009) beside docs/agents/verifying.md (1,304); triage (842) beside docs/agents/triage-labels.md (187) and issue-tracker.md (3,532); adr (196) beside docs/architecture/decisions/README.md (261); run (1,142) and debug (4,516) beside scripts/explain-failure.mjs's 9 signatures and docs/agents/session-hooks.md (2,457); e2e-and-visual (2,210) and visual-triage (1,641) beside docs/engineering/testing.md (5,238) and .claude/rules/e2e.md (759). The same operative sentence recurs across governance files — 'screenshots' in 10, 'test:changed' in 12, 'needs-triage' in 14, 'reg-suit' in 7. AGENTS.md says provider folders are adapters that 'must not introduce unique requirements', .claude/skills/README.md line 52 says a skill states how and a doc states what and why, and .claude/rules/docs.md's last bullet says long-form reasoning belongs in docs/. In the shallow history from 2026-09-08 skills changed in 2 of 364 commits while ADRs changed in 42 and guards in 23, so the twin most likely to rot is the one nobody edits.
ideas.idea: Each SKILL.md becomes frontmatter plus one screen: the trigger, the ordered pointers into the single doc that holds the body, and the commands, with scripts/check-doc-links.mjs already checking every pointer. The bodies fold into their twins — verify into docs/agents/verifying.md, new-feature into workflow.md, triage into issue-tracker.md, adr into decisions/README.md, run and debug into one docs/agents/running-and-debugging.md whose sections explain-failure.mjs's 9 signatures link to, e2e-and-visual and visual-triage into testing.md — so each operative sentence has one home and a skill links it rather than restating it. scripts/check-agents.mjs gains one invariant, a SKILL.md body over N lines fails, the way check-context-budget caps a line. The four reviewer agents keep their bodies, since a reviewer prompt has no doc twin. Afterwards the provider adapter is thin by construction, which is what roadmap.md P1's 'Provider adapters' item is asking for.
ideas.dissolves: Six duplicated playbooks and the drift between them, and the skill as a second long-form document type.
